findings.premise: The writer migration inventory covers every production path that can overwrite approval-relevant artifact state.
findings.evidence: questions.ts::recordResolution reads the whole artifact, spreads its metadata into next, then executes 'writeAtomic(loc.jsonPath, JSON.stringify(next, null, 2) ...)' and rerenders its markdown. resolve-comment.ts::resolveTargetQuestion independently reads and rewrites the whole envelope to append body.openQuestions before calling recordResolution. Both are reachable through workflow.resolveComment, including JetBrains submissions. Neither file appears in the migration inventory. These unlocked snapshots can overwrite a presentation, consumption, approval or review update even after every listed writer is migrated. findings.premise: The specified presentation metadata and approval request guarantee that the approving client approves its displayed version.
findings.evidence: Section 3.1 stores presentation timestamps and a token, but no presentedContentVersion for ordinary artifacts. requireFreshPresentation accepts only metadata and checks token/timestamp freshness. The proposed approveWorkflowTarget request contains neither an expected token nor an expected contentVersion; current reviewDecision similarly approves with only repoPath and artifactPath. Counterexample: client A displays/presents v1; a review publishes v2; client B displays/presents v2; A approves its still-open v1. The stored presentation is B's fresh token, so all specified approval checks accept v2. Locks serialize these operations but do not bind A's decision to A's view. findings.action: Define and persist the presentation's version binding for every record shape, carry the approving caller's expected presentation identity through each approval surface, and validate it against current approval-relevant content under the lock.

findings.premise: The specified timestamp comparison always detects a review published after presentation.
findings.evidence: The design rejects 'presentedAt < lastReviewWriteAt'. Existing publication paths use new Date().toISOString(), which has millisecond resolution, and both proposed helpers accept Date test seams. Presentation and a later serialized review publication can therefore have equal timestamps. The specified comparison accepts that presentation even though it preceded the review; approval performs no version comparison to catch the tie. findings.action: Use content/revision binding or explicit presentation invalidation so ordering does not depend solely on wall-clock timestamps. Define fail-closed equality behavior and test equal-time publication and rejection.

summary.prose: The daemon refuses approvals that were never presented to the human first — deterministically, not just by timestamp. Clients present the exact contentVersion they displayed (from workflow.artifactContent); workflow.present verifies that version under a per-artifact cross-worker lock against a fresh reread before stamping a single-use token. Every writer of approval-relevant state — approve, reject, daemon review publication (findings/verdicts), controller review publication (run-artifact), review resolution, code-review publication, feedback writes, present stamp, AMD transitions — runs under the same lock with a fresh reread, and review publication stamps lastReviewWriteAt at completion. approveWorkflowTarget dispatches AMD records to approveAmendment (approvedBy preserved, terminal reject kept); document-less records open via workflow.deliveryEvidence. epicHash batches require the explicit artifactIds list; overrides are present-gated; bookkeeping fields are excluded from the BUILD review fingerprint; stale-review stays non-overridable. The MCP insrc_present keeps its public { presented, notPending } contract. TUI gains an open-and-read view that presents on open; VS Code and JetBrains present on document open.
